hypotheses.author: risk
hypotheses.claim: bson@1.0.9 (CVE-2020-7610, CVSS 9.8, fix 1.1.4) is the highest-consequence finding in this repo because it is the only critical-severity advisory sitting on the app's own runtime path: owasp-nodejs-goat@1.3.0 > mongodb@2.2.36 > mongodb-core@2.1.20 > bson@1.0.9. Its computed score (43.36, Medium) understates consequence because reachability was scored present_only rather than imported, even though mongodb@2.2.36 is a direct runtime dependency.
reasons: Supported parts: F-089 shows bson@1.0.9 with CVE-2020-7610, cvss 9.8, fixed_in 1.1.4 from grype/osv-scanner/trivy (E-0157, E-0158, E-0159), and the path owasp-nodejs-goat@1.3.0 > mongodb@2.2.36 > mongodb-core@2.1.20 > bson@1.0.9 is exactly E-0155. Score 43.36 / Medium and reachability present_only / exposure runtime_internal are as stated in F-089.

The 'only critical-severity advisory on the app's own runtime path' claim is false as written. F-011 underscore@1.9.1 is severity critical (CVE-2021-23358, cvss 9.8), reachability imported, exposure runtime_network, direct path owasp-nodejs-goat@1.3.0 > underscore@1.9.1 (E-1214/E-1215/E-1216/E-1217, E-1474 require('underscore') in config/config.js), and it scores 57.24, higher than F-089's 43.36. F-001 fsevents@1.2.9 is also severity critical (confirmed_malicious, MAL-2023-462) on a runtime_internal path via forever@2.0.0 > forever-monitor@2.0.0 > chokidar@2.1.8 (E-0303), though reachability is present_only.
The 'highest-consequence finding' framing is therefore unsupported: at least two other critical-severity findings (F-011, F-001) sit on runtime paths, and F-011 outranks F-089 on the computed score.

The 'mongodb@2.2.36 is a direct runtime dependency' premise is supported (F-017 path owasp-nodejs-goat@1.3.0 > mongodb@2.2.36, E-0779; require in server.js line 11, E-1470), but the inference that bson's reachability should be 'imported' is not evidenced: no evidence record shows a require/import of bson itself, and bson is reached only through mongodb-core. F-017's own imported score applies to mongodb, not to bson.

Narrowed wording that IS supported: 'bson@1.0.9 (CVE-2020-7610, CVSS 9.8, fix 1.1.4) is a critical-severity advisory on the app's runtime path (owasp-nodejs-goat@1.3.0 > mongodb@2.2.36 > mongodb-core@2.1.20 > bson@1.0.9) whose computed score of 43.36 (Medium) reflects reachability present_only; it is not the only such critical, since underscore@1.9.1 (F-011, imported/runtime_network, 57.24) and fsevents@1.2.9 (F-001, confirmed malicious) are also critical on runtime paths.'

hypotheses.author: risk
hypotheses.claim: The bulk of the raw CVE count overstates production exposure: the critical-severity advisories in handlebars@4.0.5, json-schema@0.2.3, getobject@0.1.0, growl@1.9.2 and babel-traverse@6.11.4 are all scored reachability dev_only_unused with exposure build_or_dev, so they are build-tooling risk rather than runtime risk. Only a small set, such as underscore@1.9.1 (imported, runtime_network) and body-parser@1.18.3 (imported, runtime_network), is on the runtime path.
reasons: All five named findings match the claim exactly: F-161 handlebars@4.0.5 (CVE-2019-19919, critical, dev_only_unused, build_or_dev), F-168 json-schema@0.2.3 (CVE-2021-3918, critical, dev_only_unused, build_or_dev), F-165 getobject@0.1.0 (CVE-2020-28282, critical, dev_only_unused, build_or_dev), F-163 growl@1.9.2 (CVE-2017-16042, critical, dev_only_unused, build_or_dev), F-190 babel-traverse@6.11.4 (CVE-2023-45133, critical, dev_only_unused, build_or_dev).

The runtime examples are also correct: F-011 underscore@1.9.1 is imported / runtime_network (E-1474 require('underscore') in config/config.js) and F-019 body-parser@1.18.3 is imported / runtime_network (E-1461 require('body-parser') in server.js).

The claim is appropriately hedged ('such as', 'a small set') and does not assert an exhaustive runtime list, so it is not overstated. Note for the report: the dev-path findings are still critical-severity advisories in the lockfile; 'build-tooling risk rather than runtime risk' is a statement about scored reachability/exposure, not a claim that they are harmless.

hypotheses.author: risk
hypotheses.claim: The node:12-alpine base image is the dominant container risk and is inherited rather than app-specific: trivy reports the base OS alpine 3.15.4 as end-of-service-life (no more security updates) and the Dockerfile references node:12-alpine unpinned by digest, while the 70 vulnerable_image_package findings are OS/library packages inside that image rather than code the application authors wrote.
reasons: Supported: F-031 records trivy EOSL for node@12-alpine, 'base image OS alpine 3.15.4 is end-of-service-life (no more security updates)' (E-1285). F-075 records GR-IMG-001 'FROM node:12-alpine' at Dockerfile line 1 (E-1283), i.e. no digest pin. list_findings(type=vulnerable_image_package) returns total 70, matching the stated count, and F-002/F-006 show apk packages (libcrypto1.1@1.1.1n-r0, zlib@1.2.12-r0) whose dependency_path root is docker.io/library/node:12-alpine@sha256:4517380049fc3c9aacceae7764fcf3500354b0ac8a47e4afb35b5bbeb75b9498 (E-1306).

Overstated: 'dominant container risk' is not supported by the scores. F-031 is 50.0 and F-075 is 45.0, both Medium, and F-031's confidence is low (single scanner, 15% weight coverage, reachability unknown); F-075 is a deterministic rule with no CVE database. Several image-package findings score higher (F-002 64.73, F-006 62.69, F-008 58.18).

Overstated: 'the 70 vulnerable_image_package findings are OS/library packages inside that image rather than code the application authors wrote' is only partly evidenced. F-002 and F-006 are apk OS packages, but the list includes npm packages such as minimist@1.2.5 (F-008), form-data@2.3.2 (F-013), tar@4.4.19 (F-016), qs@6.5.2 (F-027) and npm-cli-docs@0.1.0 (F-030), which are bundled inside the node image rather than Alpine OS packages; the claim's 'OS/library' wording is loose and the 'not code the authors wrote' part is an inference not shown per finding.

Narrowed wording that IS supported: 'The node:12-alpine base image carries inherited risk: trivy reports the base OS alpine 3.15.4 as end-of-service-life (E-1285, F-031, low confidence, single scanner) and the Dockerfile references node:12-alpine without a digest pin (E-1283, F-075); 70 vulnerable_image_package findings are attributed to that image, comprising Alpine OS packages (e.g. libcrypto1.1, zlib) and npm packages bundled in the image, not to application source.'

hypotheses.author: risk
hypotheses.claim: fsevents@1.2.9 (F-001) is flagged as a malicious_package via MAL-2023-462 by osv-scanner only, while grype and trivy report it as CVE-2023-45311 with fix 1.2.11; the malicious-package classification is a single-scanner signal and should be treated as unconfirmed rather than as evidence of actual compromise.
reasons: The central premise is false: the malicious-package classification is NOT a single-scanner signal. F-001's own evidence list includes E-0305, a grype scanner_result with ref GHSA-xv2f-5jw4-v95m and excerpt 'Malware in fsevents', alongside E-0306 (osv-scanner, MAL-2023-462). F-001's confidence reasons state '2 independent scanners agree (grype, osv-scanner)' and its advisory_ids are ['GHSA-xv2f-5jw4-v95m', 'MAL-2023-462']. So grype corroborates the malware classification; only osv-scanner supplies the MAL-2023-462 id specifically.

The second premise is also wrong: grype and trivy do not 'report it as CVE-2023-45311'. E-0300 (grype) and E-0301 (osv-scanner) both carry ref GHSA-8r6j-v8pm-fqw3, not CVE-2023-45311; only E-0302 (trivy) carries CVE-2023-45311. F-045's advisory_ids are ['CVE-2023-45311', 'GHSA-8r6j-v8pm-fqw3'] with fixed_in 1.2.11 from grype, osv-scanner and trivy.

The claim conflates two distinct findings. F-001 (malicious_package, MAL-2023-462 + GHSA-xv2f-5jw4-v95m, score 57.0 Critical, override confirmed_malicious) and F-045 (vulnerable_transitive, CVE-2023-45311 + GHSA-8r6j-v8pm-fqw3, score 47.74 Medium) are separate records on the same component; the 'while' framing implies one classification displacing the other, which the data does not show.

The 'should be treated as unconfirmed rather than as evidence of actual compromise' conclusion does not follow from the cited evidence and is a judgement the evidence contradicts: F-001 carries confirmed_malicious=true and a provenance factor of 100.0. A defensible narrower statement would be that the malware advisory is corroborated by two scanners but the MAL-2023-462 id itself comes from osv-scanner only, and that F-001's score rests on 50% weight coverage (cvss, epss_kev unknown). That is not what was claimed.

Note for the report: E-1292 shows 'hasInstallScript': true at package-lock.json line 3294, which is relevant context for an install-time malware advisory and should not be omitted if the report discusses F-001.

final_message:
The report was accepted.

## Summary

**What I did:** Planned a 7-item investigation, then ran four specialists in parallel (inventory, vulnerability, container_ci, forensics), followed by `risk` to build findings, `remediation` to propose fixes, and two `verifier` passes to rule on hypotheses.

**Key results:**
- **424 components**, 418 stored findings. Three scanners (grype, trivy, osv-scanner) ran and substantially agreed.
- **Runtime-path priorities:** F-089 `bson@1.0.9` (CVE-2020-7610, 9.8, fix 1.1.4, via `mongodb@2.2.36`), F-011 `underscore@1.9.1` (critical, highest-scoring runtime finding at 57.24), F-019 `body-parser@1.18.3`, F-017 `mongodb@2.2.36`.
- **F-001 `fsevents@1.2.9`** is flagged `confirmed_malicious` by two independent scanners — the one finding that looks like actual compromise rather than age.
- **Container:** `node:12-alpine` unpinned and EOL; 145 image matches, 70 attributed to the image.
- **One real non-CVE risk:** `grunt-if` pulled from a mutable `tarball/master` URL.
- **No KEV entries**; highest EPSS 0.696 (y18n).

**Six proposals recorded, none applied** — R-001/R-003 are low-risk wins; R-006 (mongodb 2→3) and R-004 (marked 0→4) are major bumps needing human validation. Stopped at the approval gate as instructed.

**Two things worth flagging to you:**
1. **F-001 `fsevents` has no proposal** — the remediation agent ran out of calls. It's a confirmed-malicious critical and needs a human decision.
2. **Two hypotheses are stuck at `needs_more_evidence`** — the verifier rejected their original wording ("only critical on a runtime path", "dominant container risk") and approved narrower claims, but no tool in the system can edit hypothesis text. I reported only the supported facts and avoided the rejected framings. Someone with a hypothesis-edit tool should apply the narrowed wording.

The first submission was rejected for citing identifiers the gate couldn't match (scanner version numbers, action tags, a lockfile path) and for referencing unverified hypotheses; I removed those and resubmitted.

args.justification: underscore@1.9.1 is a direct runtime dependency that is imported and exposed on the runtime network path, so CVE-2021-23358 / GHSA-cf4h-3jhx-xvhq is reachable rather than theoretical. The fix to 1.12.1 is a minor bump within 1.x, which is the smallest change that clears it; app call sites should still be smoke-tested because 1.9.x to 1.12.x changed some template and iteratee edge-case behaviour.

bson@1.0.9 is pulled in only via mongodb@2.2.36 > mongodb-core@2.1.20, so it is present in the tree but not directly imported by app code. CVE-2020-7610 (CVSS 9.8) is a deserialization issue; EPSS 0.02309 and not in KEV. A patch-level bump to 1.1.4 stays within the 1.x line and is the smallest change that clears it, but it must be delivered through the mongodb dependency chain rather than by editing the lockfile by hand.

body-parser@1.18.3 is a direct runtime dependency that is imported and reachable from the network, so CVE-2024-45590 matters here. # Supply-Chain Risk Assessment — TestMote__nodegoat-20261124T113249Z

## Overall picture

This is `owasp-nodejs-goat@1.3.0`, a **deliberately vulnerable training application**. That framing matters: the app-level weaknesses (A1–A10) are intentional and are not supply-chain defects. The supply-chain picture is nonetheless poor, and it is dominated by **age, not by compromise**.

The SBOM holds **424 components** across a graph of 1480 nodes and 2295 edges, max depth 13, with 36 direct dependencies (16 runtime, 20 dev). Three independent scanners ran and substantially agreed: grype 0.121.3 (340 matches / 196 advisories), trivy 0.76.2 (325 / 206), osv-scanner 2.7.1 (313 / 196). `build_findings` produced **418 stored findings**.

The single most important structural fact: **the runtime surface is small (16 direct deps) but the dev/build tree dominates the graph** (790 unique dev packages vs 380 runtime). Raw CVE counts therefore overstate production exposure. This is recorded as **H-02, verified** by the verifier.

**No CVE in the top-20 set is in CISA KEV** (KEV catalog 2026.11.20). Highest EPSS is CVE-2020-7774 (y18n) at 0.69589 — an outlier well above its peers.

## What matters most

**1. Runtime-path criticals — the real priority.**
- **F-089 `bson@1.0.9`**, CVE-2020-7610, CVSS 9.8, fix 1.1.4. Path: `owasp-nodejs-goat@1.3.0 > mongodb@2.2.36 > mongodb-core@2.1.20 > bson@1.0.9`. Scored 43.36 (Medium) with reachability `present_only`. **H-01 is `needs_more_evidence`** — the claim that bson is the *only* critical on a runtime path was rejected by the verifier; `underscore@1.9.1` (F-011) and `fsevents@1.2.9` (F-001) are also critical on runtime paths. Confidence: high on the facts, medium on the ranking.
- **F-011 `underscore@1.9.1`**, CVE-2021-23358, critical, fix 1.12.1. Direct, `imported`, `runtime_network`, score 57.24 — the highest-scoring runtime finding.
- **F-019 `body-parser@1.18.3`**, CVE-2024-45590, high, fix 1.20.3. Direct, `imported`, `runtime_network`.
- **F-017 `mongodb@2.2.36`**, GHSA-mh5c-679w-hh4r, high, fix 3.1.13. Direct, `imported` at `server.js` line 11.

**2. A confirmed-malicious package flag.**
**F-001 `fsevents@1.2.9`** is scored Critical (57.0) as `malicious_package`, `confirmed_malicious: true`, with `MAL-2023-462` and `GHSA-xv2f-5jw4-v95m`. **Two independent scanners agree** (grype E-0305, osv-scanner E-0306) — this is *not* a single-scanner signal. A hypothesis (H-04) that it was unconfirmed was **rejected** by the verifier. Note the scanners split on the advisory id: grype and osv-scanner report GHSA-8r6j-v8pm-fqw3, trivy reports CVE-2023-45311. Fix 1.2.11. **No remediation proposal was produced for this finding** — it needs a human decision.

**3. Container base image.**
`node:12-alpine` is referenced **unpinned by digest** at `Dockerfile:1` and `Dockerfile:7`, and trivy reports the base OS **alpine 3.15.4 as end-of-service-life**. The image scan found **145 matches (11 critical, 74 high, 56 medium, 4 low)**. **70 `vulnerable_image_package` findings** are attributed to that image — Alpine OS packages *and* npm packages bundled in it — not to application source. **H-03 is `needs_more_evidence`**: the verifier rejected calling this the "dominant" container risk, since F-031 scores 50.0 and F-075 45.0 while F-002 (64.73) and F-006 (62.69) score higher. The inherited-risk framing is supported; the superlative is not.

**4. CI/CD.**
Seven unpinned GitHub Actions: `ci.yml:14` `actions/checkout@v4`; `e2e-test.yml:16` `checkout@v2`, `:21` `setup-node@v1`, `:26` `cache@v2`, `:58` `upload-artifact@v2`; `lint.yml:16` `checkout@v2`, `:21` `setup-node@v1`. Three `excessive-permissions` hits. **No `pull_request_target`, `workflow_run` or `issue_comment` triggers**, and no untrusted event data interpolated into `run:` blocks — so no script-injection path was found.

**5. One genuine non-CVE supply-chain risk.**
`grunt-if@0.2.0` is declared at `package.json:51` as `https://github.com/binarymist/grunt-if/tarball/master` — a **mutable branch ref**, sha1 integrity, dev-only, direct. The bytes fetched can change with no lockfile change. Rule GR-LOCK-001, high. The four typosquat hits (`director`, `node-eta`, `pad-stream`, `lodash.rest`) were assessed as **false positives**.

## Pending remediation proposals — HUMAN APPROVAL REQUIRED

Six proposals are recorded. **Nothing has been applied, merged or pushed.** Main is untouched.

| Proposal | Package | Change | Clears | Compatibility | Human decision |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **R-001** | underscore | 1.9.1 → 1.13.8 (direct) | F-011, F-025 | **low** — minor within major 1 | No |
| **R-003** | body-parser | 1.18.3 → 1.20.9 (direct) | F-019, F-037, F-078 | **low** — minor within major 1 | No |
| **R-002** | bson | 1.0.9 → 1.1.4 (override) | F-089, F-208 | **medium** — patch within major 1, but an override forces every consumer | Yes — override |
| **R-005** | y18n | 3.2.1 → 3.2.2 (override) | F-012 | **medium** — patch, but an override | Yes — override |

# Supply-Chain Risk Assessment — TestMote__nodegoat-20261124T113249Z

## Overall picture

This is `owasp-nodejs-goat@1.3.0`, a **deliberately vulnerable training application**. That framing matters: the app-level weaknesses (A1–A10) are intentional and are not supply-chain defects. The supply-chain picture is nonetheless poor, and it is dominated by **age, not by compromise**.

The SBOM holds **424 components** across a graph of 1480 nodes and 2295 edges, max depth 13, with 36 direct dependencies (16 runtime, 20 dev). Three independent scanners ran and substantially agreed: grype (340 matches / 196 advisories), trivy (325 / 206), osv-scanner (313 / 196). `build_findings` produced **418 stored findings**.

The single most important structural fact: **the runtime surface is small (16 direct deps) but the dev/build tree dominates the graph** (790 unique dev packages vs 380 runtime). Raw CVE counts therefore overstate production exposure.

**No CVE in the top-20 set is in CISA KEV.** Highest EPSS is CVE-2020-7774 (y18n) at 0.69589 — an outlier well above its peers.
